    "When Tim Costello was in Year 9 at school, he asked his teacher whether poverty is just something that naturally happens and can’t be avoided, like the tide or the sunrise.",
    "Looking back, he still thinks it was an important question. His conclusion is that poverty isn’t inevitable—it happens because of choices governments and societies make (their policies).",
    "The article describes Costello sitting on sand dunes at Frankston beach near his home, setting the scene for the interview.",
    "That idea he formed as a teenager shaped his whole life and career.",
    "Costello is now 69 and has spent more than 30 years working directly on issues related to poverty in Australia, which the article says has been getting worse.",
    "Over his life he has also done many other things: travelled to places affected by war and disasters, served as the mayor of St Kilda, written books, and received major public recognition.",
    "People sometimes mix him up with his brother Peter Costello, who is a well-known former government treasurer.",
    "The writer mentions that two people asked whether the interview was with the ‘Liberal’ Costello (Peter) or the ‘church’ Costello (Tim).",
    "Tim Costello is especially known as a Baptist minister and for being the CEO of the charity World Vision for 13 years."
  ]
}
```
